items.title: Every player -> GM bridge request was emitted with no recipients, so every player's socket received it (parked murder with its note, steals, plants, sabotage, crisis actions).
items.old_state: fixed in 1.2.43 (AUDIT section 2.1: emitToGms() with recipients: activeGmIds())
items.evidence: Since E31 every request goes through one waiter: scripts/bridge-table.mjs:1653 ask() -> scripts/bridge-guards.mjs:2144 bridgeRequest(); the waiter sends only to the GMs connected (bridge-guards.mjs:2120 emit with { recipients }, :2121 gmIds = activeGmIds()), and with none connected it says noGm and sends nothing (:1960-1962). A read-only text count over scripts/*.mjs without the suite's files (emits.py) found 63 places spelling socket.emit(, 5 of them with no recipients in the call: one is inside a comment (voice.mjs:575) and four are real (fog.mjs:1361, gm-bridge.mjs:111, relay-guard.mjs:1040, sync.mjs:199); none of the four is a player's request.
items.pinned_by: R201 (tier 0, scripts/tests-tier0.mjs:7669: every socket emit names its recipients but four listed ones, each held to its fields); R6
items.refutation_tried: Looked for a second road: read the four emits that name nobody; sync.mjs:199 carries a kind and public data (clock, Eclipse flag, a called assembly's token ids), no request.
items.note: The four un-addressed emits are the same four R201 lists. A real-table reading of a bridge request on another player's socket was not found; docs/dev/e58/LOCAL-REPORT.md:418 (Foundry 14.370, 16.11.2026) records that an addressed secret.card packet was not heard on a third browser's socket, which is the same mechanism.

items.title: Play a track and Reset are open to any GM, but the music's state machine and its record of what a cue interrupted live on the primary only: an assistant GM's Play leaves two records that disagree, and stale held playlists come back later.
items.old_state: listed open (minor) in section 4 after 1.2.43; named in no task (2, 3, 10 or 13) and not in b888c066's message, while section 9.1a says all 152 ids are closed - not accounted for by name
items.evidence: scripts/music-play.mjs:1098-1099 playTrack and :1179-1180 resetMusic still gate on game.user.isGM; the record `interrupted` is one browser's memory (:175). Every road that clears or reconciles it except resetMusic itself (:1186) is behind enabled(), which is primary-only (:381-382; apply :398-413 and :445-455, the watchers :934 and :1008, resumeAmbient :1035). On the primary, a cue another GM started is recorded with held [] (:958-993: the other GM paused everything first), so when the state moves, the primary lets go of nothing the other GM flagged (:448-454). A second GM's later Reset resumes its own record's held list with no test that the room is silent (:1210-1217; the silence test at :1211 guards only the no-record case), and its later Play reuses the stale list and pauses nothing (:1123-1130).
items.pinned_by: none found (no test or scenario calls playTrack or resetMusic; scenario 87 part C drives a second GM's map writes only)
items.still_wrong: A second GM presses Play on a cue in the Sound window, the time of day moves to a state with another playlist (the primary cuts the cue and starts that playlist), then the second GM presses Reset: its browser resumes the playlist it paused before, and the table hears two playlists until the next state change.
items.refutation_tried: Looked for a gate or a forward to the primary on the Sound window's Play tab (scripts/sound-panel.mjs:277-287: none), for a decision in docs/dev and the release notes (none found), and for what already covers the simple case: the held flag on the playlist document (music-play.mjs:60-67, :790-795) lets the primary's own Reset give back what another GM paused when nothing else plays, and crossfade clears the flag on a playlist it starts (:558).

Still there: the rule is still 'timestamp greater than the read stamp' (:147) and the thread is sorted by timestamp (:113-117), and the stamps of one thread come from several senders; postSecret creates the document with no timestamp of its own (scripts/secret.mjs:1190-1196), so each is whatever Foundry stamps.

new_observations.what: 'Present for everyone - a Monokuma's player is at the same table' stands above code that draws no Stop on a Monokuma's sheet (E49 B2) or a Spectator's (E92 C5). scripts/safeword.mjs:272 likewise still lists the spectator among those who may call it, while a Spectator has no control on screen for it.

new_observations.title: Two presses of the safeword key open two confirmation windows
new_observations.what: Each key-down opens a new modal window; nothing holds it to one. Recorded on Foundry 14.370 in docs/dev/e58/LOCAL-REPORT.md:420 ('a fast double press opens two'). A second Stop inside the repeat window posts no second card, so the effect is a spare window.
